title: Research optimal OBS receiving-side AND encoder settings to maximize received quality from a USB ...
objective: Research optimal OBS receiving-side AND encoder settings to maximize received quality from a USB 3.0 HDMI capture card and the optimal live-stream encoder for a Windows 11 laptop running OBS to livestream 1080p60. GOALS: (1) On the laptop, in the Video Capture Device source properties: Resolution/FPS Type = Custom and exactly 1080p / 60; the Video Format options reported by generic USB3 UVC cards (MJPEG, YUY2/YUYV, NV12, H.264). Determine which is uncompressed (YUY2 = full 4:2:2, ~3 Gbps over USB3) and gives best quality, vs which compressed formats deliver artifacts; Color Space = 709; Color Range = Full (0-255) vs Limited (16-235): which the cheap generic cards advertise by default and which the user should choose; whether 'Device default' vs 'Custom' matters; deactivate buffering; disable OBS-side deinterlacing/scaling; use the Configure / Crossbar / Video Proc Amp controls to disable auto-exposure/auto-gain/auto-white-balance to prevent brightness flicker. HOW to verify the card delivers true 60 not 30-doubled (OBS Stats Capture fps, dropped-frame counters, a 60fps test pattern). (2) Encoder: if laptop has NVIDIA GPU use NVENC H.264 or HEVC; recommend CQP quality-based for quality priority (concrete CQP value for 1080p60 livestream, around 20-24), keyframe interval 2s, profile High, P5/P6 preset (Quality), multipass two-passes-quarter-res, psychovisual tuning on; OR CBR bitrate recommendation for 1080p60 livestream (~6-9 Mbps Twitch, ~12-18+ Mbps YouTube). If AMD use AMF H.264/HEVC. If no dGPU use x264 'veryfast/faster' preset tradeoffs. Mention Twitch 1080p60 bitrate ceilings (Twitch recommends 6000 Kbps, allow up to ~8000 for affiliates/partners). CONCLUDE with a concrete settings checklist for receive + encode to maximize quality. Cite OBS docs, the EposVox NVENC guide, r/OBS, Twitch/YouTube guidelines.
